text:
B: Hi. Can you hear me?
A: Erm, yeah, yeah I can. Hi. Can you hear me alright?
B: Yes, fine. I'm Greta. Peterborough.
A: Oh, I'm Kerry. I'm in Lowestoft, so sort of, erm, the other end of the region, I suppose.
B: By the sea, yes? I have been once. It was very windy.
A: It's always windy. I walk along the seafront most days and some days you sort of can't stand up straight, do you know what I mean.
B: Mm. That puzzle at the start, did you finish it?
A: Erm, no. I got stuck on the one with the shapes. I don't know if I was doing it right. Did you?
B: I finished, but I think I did it wrong. The instructions were badly written, to be honest. Somebody designed that page in a hurry.
A: Oh, right. I just thought it was me being thick.
B: No, no. The font was too small, everything was grey on grey. It's my job, so it annoys me.
A: Sorry, what do you do?
B: Graphic design. Part-time, at a print company. Menus, leaflets, sometimes a van. Last month a funeral director wanted Comic Sans on the side of his van. I said no. My boss said yes.
A: Oh no. On a hearse?
B: Not the hearse, the other van. Still. People will see it at a funeral and think it's a children's party.
A: That's quite funny actually. Sorry. Not funny for you.
B: It's a bit funny. What do you do?
A: Erm, I'm not working at the minute. I was in a warehouse, picking, for six years, but they cut the shifts last spring. So I'm sort of looking. Is that alright? Like, is that what you meant?
B: Of course. There's no wrong answer. Is it hard, finding something?
A: Yeah, a bit. I'm applying for cleaning, shelf-stacking, early shifts really. I don't mind hard work, I just don't want to be on the phone all day. I get, erm, nervous in interviews and that.
B: Me too, honestly. I hate interviews. I always say something stupid and then I think about it for a week.
A: Yeah, that's exactly it. You go over it in bed, don't you.
B: Exactly. Erm, I saw a cat in your... no, sorry, that was plant. Spider plant?
A: Oh, yeah, that's my spider plant. It's finally growing, it's got babies on it now. I was quite chuffed. No cat, I'm not allowed in the flat.
B: I have a cat, Pilkis. He's grey. He knocked my coffee onto my keyboard last month, so now the E key sticks.
A: Oh no. My mum's dog does stuff like that, eats tea towels. What's... sorry, how do you say his name?
B: Pilkis. It means grey in Lithuanian. Not very creative from a designer, I know.
A: No, I like it. It's nice and simple.
B: What do you do when you're not looking for jobs?
A: Erm, walking mostly, 'cause it's free. Charity shops. I got a coat last week for four quid, a proper wool one.
B: Four pounds? That's good. I found a seventies wool coat on Vinted for twelve and I was very proud.
A: Twelve's still good though. What colour?
B: Brown, sort of camel. It smells a bit of somebody's grandmother, but in a nice way.
A: Mine did too. I think they all do. I just hung it by the radiator for a few days.
B: Good tip. Do you watch...
